# 5. Conceptual Principles

## 5.1. AP-001 — Documentation as Knowledge

Documentation shall represent organized knowledge through logical entities, identified sources and applicable contracts. A file is a representation, not automatically a registered capability or a complete knowledge system. Normalized sources and functional files contribute within their respective scopes; DF defines documentary requirements while an applicable process produces/manages representations.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess purpose, actual source organization, relationships and coverage. The principle creates neither a document component nor proof that every file contributes complete or consistent knowledge.

---

## 5.2. AP-002 — Explicit Architecture

Architectural decisions shall identify the subject, scope, responsible owners, assumptions, applicable contracts and rationale explicitly. Significant allocation, classification, identity or required-contract changes require previous/new mapping and affected editions before propagation. Record unresolved decisions or missing evidence rather than treating an implicit label, arrow or directory as authority.

**Evidence boundary:** Examine actual decision/owner/reference records and limits. Explicit documentation proves neither approval nor complete implementation; derived summaries preserve authoritative provenance.

---

## 5.3. AP-003 — Technology Independence

Architectural definitions shall avoid prescribing technology unless an explicit integration constraint requires it. Logical identity, classification and domain meaning are distinct from filenames, formats, repositories and storage technology. Actual implementations still require representations, adapters, interfaces and executors under their applicable contracts.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess declared technology constraints and actual representation/adapter compatibility. Conceptual independence does not guarantee every format/tool is suitable, an implementation exists or technologies can evolve without consumer impact.

---

## 5.4. AP-004 — Single Source of Truth

Each semantic concept or authoritative record shall have one identified responsible owner within its declared domain/scope. Metadata Dictionary defines descriptor meaning while Identity, Classification and Governance retain their domain semantics. Traceable summaries, catalogs and projections may repeat derived values with source-edition provenance and refresh/state limits without acquiring competing authority.

**Evidence boundary:** Check responsible definition/record sources, derived-copy provenance and unresolved conflicts. Logical single authority does not require one physical copy, a universal Registry route or a complete canonical catalog merely from this principle.

---

## 5.5. AP-005 — Semantic Consistency

Consuming representations shall preserve applicable owner meanings and identify subjects/qualified contexts. Controlled aliases and historic vocabulary retain explicit mappings; unqualified overloads or competing meanings are recorded and reconciled. Metadata represents domain values, Schema organizes references, Profile constrains usage and Instance provides values under one effective Profile without redefining semantics.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess actual definitions, profiles, represented values and consumer scope. This principle does not manufacture missing Element/Profile records or prove consistency of unseen sources.

---

# 6. Structural Principles

## 6.1. AP-006 — Separation of Responsibilities

Each registered capability shall have a defined primary semantic responsibility and primary allocation. Explicit collaboration, cross-cutting participation, shared check domains and traceable projections are permitted while preserving owner boundaries. Reviews may use Validation/Consistency Verification results without acquiring their rule ownership or approval authority.

**Evidence boundary:** Check primary owner/consumer contracts and actual support interactions. Prevent competing semantics rather than prohibiting every overlap of supporting work; no new capability or reassignment is inferred from a concern or directory.

---

## 6.2. AP-007 — Layered Architecture

Structural allocation shall follow Architectural Layers:seven areas are Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation and Integration. Foundation/Architecture supply supporting definitions; the supplied 23 capabilities retain their 4/4/5/5/5 allocation. Five conceptual concerns—Knowledge, Documentation, Governance, Discovery and Preservation—are a different view.

**Evidence boundary:** For required cross-Layer consumption, record consumer→provider contract/scope/source editions and apply the declared support order:the provider precedes its consumer. Same-Layer requirements, including Knowledge Graph→Relationships and Workflow→Policies, need explicit interfaces/ownership and cycle assessment. There is no obligation to consume every earlier provider or an adjacent serial service chain. Genuine required cycles are prohibited in the governed scope and remain visible for reconciliation; no projection/reference label hides them. Changing constraints requires assessed architectural revision, not an arbitrary upward exception. These rules certify neither a full graph nor implemented layer services.

---

## 6.3. AP-008 — Modular Design

Components shall preserve coherent boundaries and compatible provider contracts where feasible. Separate areas or documents may still require coordinated content/descriptor, owner/consumer or release changes. Independent evolution is an assessed objective under actual dependencies, not an unconditional guarantee.

**Evidence boundary:** Map affected exact editions, provider compatibility and transition evidence. A new component or module label alone proves neither independent release nor operational modularity.

---

## 6.4. AP-009 — Explicit Relationships

Applicable connections shall be explicitly typed with identified endpoints and provenance. Distinguish documentary authority references, semantic associations, representation/projection, navigation, required consumption and execution. A required edge names consumer, provider, contract, scope and responsible source editions; physical directories, names and visual order alone establish no edge.

**Evidence boundary:** Check actual connection records and resolvable endpoints. Preserve genuine requirements/cycles visibly and reconcile conflicting owner contracts; do not rename an indispensable provider as navigation to create apparent acyclicity. This principle imposes no nonempty relationship list on every file.

---

## 6.5. AP-010 — Stable Identity

Normalized documents shall preserve valid permanent logical identity under the applicable Domain+Identifier allocation/preservation contract. Identifier representation, current classification, title, Version/Revision, Status and physical location are distinct facts. Existing valid DF-SSS-NNN allocations do not automatically change with Family/Type or path; necessary migration needs a mapped assessed identity change.

**Evidence boundary:** Apply the functional-file exclusion in §3 first:README.md, CHANGELOG.md and ArchitecturalMilestones.md require no normalized ID by this principle. Assess actual uniqueness/resolution and collision evidence; no 000 functional identity, missing allocation or universal generation algorithm is invented.

---

# 8. Evolution Principles

## 8.1. AP-015 — Incremental Evolution

Prefer incremental architectural improvement where it can meet actual requirements while preserving compatible meaning. A necessary larger or foundational change can be justified when incremental alternatives cannot adequately satisfy identified responsibilities or constraints.

**Evidence boundary:** Record previous/new contracts, alternatives/rationale, affected owners/consumers, dependencies and transition/verification evidence. Avoid disruption where feasible without an absolute ban on justified incompatible reconciliation.

---

## 8.2. AP-016 — Backward Compatibility

Preserve compatible meaning and provider/consumer contracts where feasible. Necessary incompatible changes shall be explicitly justified with affected exact editions, previous/new mappings, reference/identity effects, transition evidence and verification limits. Compatibility is assessed from contracts, not from names, folder layout or a Version label alone.

**Evidence boundary:** For this working document review, compatible correction retains Version; compatible additive capability increments minor; incompatible contract change increments major and resets minor to 0. Every changed persisted edition increments Revision monotonically across Version changes. Validation of unchanged source changes neither coordinate and is tracked centrally. Domain-specific entity numbering requires its own qualified owner; no completed consumer rollout is inferred.

---

## 8.3. AP-017 — Extensibility

Introduce a new capability or source role only for a demonstrated need with defined owner responsibility, primary allocation, typed interactions and consumer impact. Reuse or extend existing contracts where feasible. Necessary changes to foundations, responsibilities or interfaces are permitted through the assessed evolution process in AP-015/016 and §14; extension-only is not an absolute prohibition on foundational revision.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess whether existing meaning/functionality changes, actual dependencies and transition evidence. A new capability is not assumed harmless and need not create another Layer. No component, Metadata Element, Profile or specification is fabricated merely to make an extension appear complete.

---

## 8.4. AP-018 — Architectural Stability

Preserve coherent conceptual boundaries and compatible owner meanings where feasible. Implementation technologies can evolve under applicable representation/provider/consumer contracts; their independence is not guaranteed by conceptual separation. Necessary semantic changes retain source history and explicit compatibility/version transition.

**Evidence boundary:** Assess actual contracts, affected editions and integration/adapter constraints. Stability is a controlled design objective, not foundation immutability, harmless extension or a guarantee of unchanged semantics for every future edition.

---

# 14. Future Evolution

New or modified principles require demonstrated architectural need, explicit scope/rationale, previous/new rule mapping and identified owners/consumer source editions before propagation. Preserve conceptual integrity and compatible meaning where feasible; necessary foundational/contract changes are assessed and justified, not categorically forbidden by an extension-only rule.

Evaluate applicability, required dependencies, reference/identity effects, implementation constraints and compatibility/transition evidence. Preserve AP IDs/titles/category history where meanings evolve; new principles would require their own controlled allocation, and none is allocated here. Incremental alternatives and reasons for unavoidable disruption remain documented.

Apply the document-edition numbering contract in AP-016:changed persisted editions increment Revision monotonically, necessary incompatible contracts increment major/reset minor 0, and unchanged-source validation leaves coordinates intact. A Version number or local correction proves no integrated consumer rollout, global graph, implementation maturity, approval or new Baseline.

---

# 4. Scope

The component's scope includes identity concepts, models, elements/schema, constraints, identity lifecycle, validation, governance, typed relationships, assessed extensibility, specifications and examples. Detailed sources retain their responsibilities; this architecture does not invent a canonical merged field catalog or certify all peer requirements.

For applicable normalized documents, logical identity remains associated with the same document across ordinary content/descriptor, classification, representation, repository and document-edition changes. Exact edition coordinates, document Status, identity-record assignment/preservation/retirement evidence, maturity and Baseline membership are separate facts. A mutable state record is not a replacement for the stable identity key.

Unassigned concerns a pre-allocation subject, not an already assigned Domain+Identifier key. Retirement preserves allocated-number reservation, document association/history and reference interpretation; it does not guarantee a running resolver or retrievable content. Document lifecycle and identity-record lifecycle can have distinct subjects/contracts. The source does not prescribe a universal transition or permission graph.

DID-003/004/005/006/010/014 currently disagree on reference cardinality, mandatory State/Canonical Reference fields and identity state terminology. Those actual claims are preserved in §12.3 for full owner cycles. The architectural distinctions here neither merge incompatible schemas nor silently remove/add their mandatory fields. No Metadata Dictionary Element, Profile or canonical state record is fabricated.

---

# 7. Core Architectural Characteristics

Within its declared allocation/preservation contract, an assigned logical identity shall be unique for the document in its domain, stable through normal evolution, and never reassigned to a different document. Domain qualification is required to interpret uniqueness; an identifier string alone is not universally unique across unregistered domains.

Immutability concerns the assigned Domain+Identifier key under its applicable contract, not every mutable record about that identity. Identity-state evidence, references, location, descriptors and exact-edition coordinates can evolve under their own owner rules without automatically replacing the key. References and aliases interpret an existing logical document; they do not license another document to reuse its identity. Allocated and retired identities remain reserved.

Preserve valid assigned identity during ordinary classification, repository, format, lifecycle and edition changes. If a necessary authorized schema/ID migration would change an otherwise immutable representation/allocation contract, first assess and explicitly reconcile the governing previous/new rules with responsible identity/domain sources. Record old→new mappings, same-document continuity, aliases/reservations, collisions, historical/reference/context effects, exact source editions, affected consumers and transition verification before coordinated application. Preserve original representations and historical immutable snapshot selections; never retarget old members or reassign retired allocations to another document. No blanket permission for arbitrary identity changes or two contradictory governing rules for one operation is introduced. This localized UPDATE performs no migration.

Long-term understandable/referenceable identity is a requirement and design objective supported by qualified domain/canonicalization and actual preservation/resolution evidence. It guarantees neither universally understood bare strings nor future content availability. Exact-edition references additionally identify the intended Version/Revision and relevant bytes/context; logical identity alone selects neither an exact edition nor Baseline membership.

---

# 9. Component Relationships

The following are scoped architectural contract declarations for documentary uses. They do not establish an operational service call, every-component routing requirement or complete dependency graph.

| Consumer | Provider | Required contract/use | Source/scope boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metadata | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document described | DID-009 §5.1 declaration; descriptive values retain their own semantic owners |
| Classification | Document Identity | Identity of the normalized document being classified | DID-009 §5.2; category/definition entity identity is a separate qualified contract |
| Templates | Document Identity | Identity of normalized Template documentation/document instances | DID-009 §5.3; Template definition/instance keys are not automatically DF document IDs |
| Registry | Document Identity | Logical document identity for a document catalog entry | DID-001 §9.4; source-edition provenance and exact lookup context required |
| Relationships | Document Identity | Identity of document endpoints | DID-001 §9.5; other endpoint kinds use their own domain contracts |
| Knowledge Graph | Document Identity | Logical document node identity | ARC-005 §12; typed edges remain Relationships records, not document identities |
| Baselines | Document Identity | Logical member identity | ARC-005 §12; exact edition/descriptive/context evidence additionally required |
| Workflow | Document Identity | Identified normalized document subject | DID-009 §6.1; applicable transition execution remains with the actual process |

## 9.1. Metadata

Identity identifies the logical document; Metadata defines/represents descriptors and owner meanings. Dictionary/Schema/Profile/Instance roles remain separate under one effective Profile. Identity data can be represented descriptively without transferring identity semantics or creating missing Metadata Element/catalog records.

**Unresolved reciprocal declarations:** supplied README states Document Identity→Metadata for descriptive concepts, while DID-009 §§5/10 states Metadata→Document Identity and no dependency on consuming components. Both source claims remain visible as required-dependency evidence pending owner/context/interface reconciliation. Distinguish core identity meaning from identity-record descriptor use, but do not silently downgrade a genuinely required contract into navigation or declare the apparent cycle resolved. Different stated uses alone do not prove operational independence or global acyclicity. Full Metadata/DID source cycles must establish the actual required scopes and cycle treatment under ARC-004.

## 9.2. Classification

Classification owns category meanings and uses identity when categorizing a normalized document. Current Family/Type/Component labels are independent from stable allocation series and do not automatically reconstruct an assigned valid ID. Classification definitions and their own lifecycle/keys are different subjects from document editions; their actual identity contracts need qualification. Nominal CLS-003/CLS-001 collision reconciliation remains scheduled, not corrected by this source.

## 9.3. Templates

Templates owns reusable documentary structures and definition/instance contracts. A normalized document describing or applying a Template can require document identity; Template entities and graph/relationship identifiers are not thereby allocated normalized document IDs. Templates consumes appropriate owner meanings without redefining document identity, Metadata or Classification. Source presence and using a Template prove neither consistency nor approved publication.

## 9.4. Registry

Registry catalogs/looks up identified documentary entities or editions under declared provenance and freshness/current-historical-snapshot context. It does not redefine identity. A document lookup needs its domain/canonical key; an exact-edition lookup additionally needs edition/context evidence. No universal Registry intermediary, implemented resolver or persistent content availability is implied.

## 9.5. Relationships

Relationships owns typed connection records and provenance; Document Identity owns the contract for document endpoints. Other endpoint kinds use their own qualified identity domains. Canonical document reference validity requires the intended document/edition context and actual evidence; logical reference preservation does not imply live-content retrieval. Required edges remain required even when their data comes through a projection; a reference label cannot conceal a genuine cycle.

## 9.6. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph projects identified entities and Relationships records with source/edition provenance and refresh limits. Document nodes use document identity; graph edges or non-document entities need appropriate other contracts. Projections do not create competing identity/relationship authority or certify complete network correctness. No Registry→Graph→Baseline execution chain is prescribed.

## 9.7. Governance

For a document endpoint use the intended qualified document or exact edition/context under §4.4; other typed endpoints follow their own contracts. No rule here forces all possible associations to be document-to-document. Mutable connections do not redefine the key, and canonical endpoints alone do not prove a valid connection or permanently available target.

---

## 7.3. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph owns logical node/edge projection and representation contracts; storage/runtime technologies remain implementation choices. Knowledge Graph→Document Identity for document-node meaning and Knowledge Graph→Relationships for typed connections are selected required contracts in ARC-005§12. Neither is eliminated by calling the graph a projection.

Keep authoritative keys/connection sources distinct from projected records/properties. Nodes and properties may change while preserving intended qualified identity. Retain source edition/context, derivation, provenance, freshness and observed limitations. Projection does not allocate a new document identity, acquire connection authority or prove every peer representation is synchronized.

---

## 7.4. Navigation

Navigation uses intended identity and context to locate an applicable document or edition under its navigation contract. It can derive links and presentation records while preserving authoritative target meaning; the received prohibition on creating identity information means no competing allocation/semantic invention, not a ban on derived representation. Navigation does not guarantee successful current retrieval, require a universal Registry route or authorize silent retargeting.

---

## 7.5. Search

Search→Document Identity is the required identification contract for document-targeting search results. Other indexed entities retain their own endpoint contracts. Search owns query/result behavior, not document-key meaning. Record actual indexed source editions/context, target interpretation, freshness and result/retrieval observations. An index match does not prove allocation, complete population coverage, full identity validity or future availability.

---

# 8. Relationships with Automation Components

Automation is an area, not a single component. The five retained headings map to canonical ARC-005§8 components below. Capability definitions do not establish an installed executor. Actual execution records exact inputs/outputs, source editions/bytes, responsible rules, contributor/executor, authorization where applicable, checks, observations and limits. Never infer missing identity/status/approval facts from generated output.

---

## 8.1. Validation

Received Validation → registered Validation. Evaluate applicable identity rules against the exact subject/domain, source editions/context and coverage. DID-007 distinguishes Valid, Invalid, Inconsistent and Unresolvable outcomes; unexecuted/partial/conflicted checks do not justify unconditional full validity. Separate nonmutating evaluation from writing a result record or an independently authorized correction. Validation is not formal approval.

---

## 8.2. Metadata Generation

Received Metadata Generation → registered Metadata Generator. Generate descriptor representations from actual authoritative source facts/rules and associate them with the intended qualified document/edition/context. Metadata retains descriptor meaning. Preserve derivation and actual input/output bytes, contributors and checks; do not invent allocation, missing metadata definitions, lifecycle state or approval evidence.

---

## 8.3. Registry Generation

Received Registry Generation → registered Registry Generator. Derive registration entries for intended existing document keys from actual source editions and Registry contracts. Registry owns the entries, not the generator or identity semantic owner. Record scope, input/output provenance, reservations/collision evidence when actually examined and freshness. Emission is not allocation, global completeness or approval.

---

## 8.4. Consistency Verification

Received Consistency Verification → registered Consistency Verification (ARC-005§8.5). Compare actual repositories/assets/records under exact applicable rule/source editions and population coverage. Record contradictions, missing evidence, observations and limits; local consistency does not prove global conformance, a complete acyclic graph or authority to repair records.

---

## 8.5. Documentation Generators

Received Documentation Generators → registered Documentation Generator (ARC-005§8.4). Generate document representations under applicable template/source contracts while preserving existing qualified identity and cumulative evidenced contributions. A new document requires its own actual allocation decision; generation cannot invent an identity, attribute an unauthored contribution or inherit approval/Baseline membership. Record exact inputs, outputs and checks.

---

# 9. Relationships with Integration Components

Integration is an area; these five received examples map to ARC-005§9 components without inventing additional registered components or implemented adapters.

| Received example | Registered component | Contract / execution boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Source Control | Source Control Integration | Map actual repository representations/history to intended document/edition; repository locator is not identity |
| CI/CD platforms | CI/CD Integration | Exchange actual input/output/check evidence; a pipeline result is not architectural approval |
| IDE extensions | IDE Integration | Preserve intended key/context in editing/navigation; an editor action grants no allocation permission |
| Documentation platforms | Documentation Platform Integration | Preserve authoritative identity and exact edition/context across representations; publication needs its actual decision |
| AI-based services | AI Integration | Record actual sources, generated outputs and contributions; never fabricate identity, authority, state or validation facts |

Actual adapters/executors require their applicable authorization, exact source/output editions/bytes, mappings, checks, observations and limits. Logical identity meaning is technology independent; legitimate format/interface constraints and actual external requirements still matter. Necessary representation migration follows §4.2. No adapter, service, allocation, synchronization guarantee or automatic approval is created here.

---

# 10. Dependency Overview

The received overview mixed semantic provision, component collaboration and area order. Replace its untyped arrows with this typed view while preserving all nine original labels. It is not a mandatory serial pipeline.

<!-- original-section-view: 10 -->
**Previously unnamed view in §10 — Scoped dependency and collaboration overview.**

| Original subject | Kind / relation to Document Identity | Direction / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Document Identity | Semantic owner/provider and actual declared consumer | Provides document-key meaning; reciprocal Metadata requirement remains unresolved |
| Metadata | Descriptor owner / required consumer and provider claims | Metadata→Document Identity (§5.1.1); Document Identity→Metadata (functional README) |
| Classification | Category owner / required document-key consumer | Classification→Document Identity for applicable classified document (§5.2.1) |
| Registry | Registration owner / required document-key consumer | Registry→Document Identity for document registrations (§7.1) |
| Relationships | Connection owner / document endpoint consumption | Relationship semantics remain with Relationships; intended document endpoints use identity contracts (§7.2) |
| Knowledge Graph | Logical projection owner / required document-node consumer | Knowledge Graph→Document Identity; typed connections also require Relationships (§7.3) |
| Governance | Area: Workflow, Policies, Reviews, Baselines | Documentary state/rule/review/exact-snapshot contracts, not one component or an executor (§6) |
| Automation | Area: five registered components | Applicable checking/generation/verification contracts, not obligatory routing (§8) |
| Integration | Area: five registered components | Actual scoped exchange/adapter contracts, not an obligatory final stage (§9) |
<!-- end-original-section-view -->

Required dependency direction is consumer→provider. Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation and Integration form the architectural support order under ARC-004/005; they are not a universal serial chain. Same-Layer required contracts need explicit scope/interfaces and no required cycles. Semantic ownership, documentary reference, projection, data flow and operational execution are different relations.

Selected actual requirements also include Registry→Metadata (descriptors), Knowledge Graph→Relationships (typed connections), Workflow→Metadata (state/edition), Workflow→Policies (rules), Baselines→Document Identity (logical member) and Baselines→Metadata (exact edition/pinned context), under ARC-004§§12–13 and ARC-005§12/selected component clauses. These are selected declarations, not a complete graph or supplied implementation interfaces.

The former blanket claim “Document Identity has no dependency on the consuming components” is not accepted as the current general rule: the actual README declares the reciprocal Metadata requirement. Preserve both claims and exact source evidence; responsible owner/interface reconciliation is pending. Core-versus-descriptor naming, changing relation labels or omitting an indispensable edge does not prove acyclicity. No global DAG certification follows from this source-local correction. Received view text/digest remains external evidence at this original section.

# 3. Constraint Principles

The seven received principle subjects remain as scoped requirements, not new architectural principle identifiers or guaranteed outcomes.

| Original principle | Qualified meaning / evidence boundary |
|---|---|
| mandatory | Applicable responsible requirements bind the declared conformance claim; unresolved mandatory authority is not silently waived |
| technology independent | Preserve logical meaning across applicable implementations; explicit representation/integration constraints remain |
| implementation independent | Owner semantics are distinct from runtime choices; actual executors still meet contract/evidence obligations |
| repository independent | Location/custody does not define the key; real movement/reference/freshness effects require assessment |
| deterministic | Equivalent pinned inputs, rules and relevant observation context receive stable rule interpretation; disclose live or nondeterministic dependencies |
| verifiable | State exact subject, applicable rules, artifacts/editions/context, executor, checks, observations, coverage and limits |
| permanent | Preserve assigned same-document association, reservations and historical interpretation; rule evolution is separately governed and live content is not guaranteed |

These principles do not create a context-free checker, permission to mutate identities or evidence of universal interoperability.

---

# 4. Identity Constraints

The five original Identity constraints retain DID-C-001–005 and their rationale associations. The labels are retained source-local constraint identifiers, not new normalized document IDs or newly established global allocations.

---

## 4.1. DID-C-001 — Identity Existence

An applicable assigned normalized logical document shall have one governing document identity under its declared document/domain contract. Pre-allocation is a different subject; this requirement does not assert that an unassigned key already exists.

Functional exclusions in §1 apply. Copies, files, exact editions and Metadata/Classification/Template entities are not automatically additional logical documents or required DF allocations. Actual assignment requires its responsible decision and collision/reservation/history evidence; recognition or registration alone is not allocation.

---

### 4.1.1. Rationale

A governing assigned key supports unambiguous recognition of the intended logical document. Scoped applicability avoids inventing keys for pre-allocation subjects, excluded functional files or other entities.

---

## 4.2. DID-C-002 — Identity Permanence

Preserve the assigned qualified key's association with the same logical document under its governing contract through ordinary content, classification, location, representation and edition/status evolution. Historical association and allocated/retired reservations remain preserved after active use ends.

Permanence does not guarantee perpetual content retrieval or freeze every supporting record. Necessary contract/representation transitions require the prior/new reconciliation protocol in §12; no reassignment to another document or historical exact-snapshot retargeting is authorized.

---

### 4.2.1. Rationale

Stable same-document association and retained provenance support long-term historical recognition. Actual target interpretation, reference validity and live retrieval remain separately assessed facts.

---

## 4.3. DID-C-003 — Identity Immutability

Immutability concerns the assigned Domain+Identifier key and same-document association under the governing contract, not every state/reference/descriptor/registration/projection record. Ordinary evolution shall preserve that key while responsible supporting records may change.

A necessary contract or representation migration first requires §12 prior/new authority, owner/consumer, mapping/reservation/history and reference/exact-snapshot continuity assessment. This is not blanket permission for arbitrary key/domain mutation, retired-key reuse or rewriting historical evidence. No migration is performed by this source.

---

### 4.3.1. Rationale

Stable key interpretation supports reference continuity. It does not guarantee every actual connection remains valid or that live content is always available; exact context and observed evidence remain required.

---

## 4.4. DID-C-004 — Identity Uniqueness

Different logical documents shall not receive the same full qualified Domain+Identifier key within its governing allocation/canonicalization contract. Assess actual assignments, intended subjects, domain authority, canonical/alias interpretation, population and current/historical collision/reservation coverage.

Copies, repeated registration/projection records, legitimate aliases and exact editions about the same logical document do not alone constitute duplicate allocations. Equal numeric suffixes in different registered series do not alone collide. Syntax or a partial index is not proof of global uniqueness; missing evidence is reported with its limits.

---

### 4.4.1. Rationale

Qualified uniqueness prevents competing assignments and ambiguous canonical interpretation within an identified domain. An actual collision claim needs actual conflicting subject/assignment evidence, not mere repeated text or copies.

---

## 4.5. DID-C-005 — Identity Non-Reusability

Allocated and retired keys shall never be reassigned to another logical document. Preserve original same-document association, retirement decision/scope, reservation history and intended historical interpretation. Retirement ends active use in its declared scope without releasing the key.

A gap, absent index entry, missing reservation history or unavailable content establishes neither availability nor an observed reassignment. Preserve actual evidence and limits; do not silently allocate, retire or repair a key.

---

### 4.5.1. Rationale

Non-reuse protects historical association and intended reference interpretation. Historical interpretation is an obligation; permanent validity of every connection and perpetual live retrieval are not guaranteed.

---

# 5. Identifier Constraints

The three original Identifier constraints retain DID-C-006–008. Distinguish qualified semantic key, canonical rendering, legitimate aliases and resolver/location records under the responsible domain contract.

---

## 5.1. DID-C-006 — Canonical Identifier

Each applicable assigned document identity shall have one canonical identifier interpretation/representation under its governing domain rules. An unqualified rendering is not a universally unique key across domains. Legitimate aliases or copies may represent the same intended qualified identity without becoming competing canonical allocations.

For this corpus the identity domain is Documentation Framework, represented by DF. The canonical identifier follows DF-SSS-NNN: SSS is a registered uppercase three-letter stable allocation series and NNN is a positive three-digit allocation001–999. 000 is not allocated. Series codes do not recalculate from current Family, Type, Component, path, edition or status. Gaps prove no availability; allocated/retired numbers remain reserved. At999, register a traceable unused continuation series rather than widen syntax or recycle numbers. Other domains require their own explicit contracts.

Actual new allocation needs responsible series/domain authority and collision/reservation/history checks with declared coverage. This source registers no series, alias or new identity.

---

### 5.1.1. Rationale

One responsible canonical interpretation supports consistent qualified identification. Actual representation, alias and source/context evidence is needed; a canonical label or matching syntax alone proves neither uniqueness nor correct resolution.

---

## 5.2. DID-C-007 — Identifier Stability

Preserve the assigned canonical identifier and same-document association through ordinary document evolution under its governing contract. Changes to Family/Type/Component, title, content, Version/Revision, Status, repository or format do not reconstruct the stable allocation series/key.

Legitimate derived records may change without key reallocation. Any necessary representation/contract transition requires §12 prior/new owner/consumer and continuity assessment before coordinated application; old representations, reservations and immutable historical snapshots remain preserved.

---

### 5.2.1. Rationale

Stable interpreted keys support consumer continuity and interoperability. Actual compatible interfaces, representation mappings and transition checks determine observed compatibility; stability alone guarantees no complete implementation outcome.

---

## 5.3. DID-C-008 — Identifier Uniqueness

Within the declared governing domain/canonicalization contract, an identifier's canonical interpretation shall identify one intended logical document identity. Evaluate full qualified keys and actual assignments, not bare suffixes or assumed global uniqueness of strings.

Aliases must map traceably to their intended qualified subject under responsible rules. Ambiguous or conflicting interpretations remain observations requiring owner resolution. A unique intended interpretation is distinct from a successful running resolver or current content availability.

---

### 5.3.1. Rationale

Unambiguous qualified interpretation avoids competing targets. Actual lookup/resolution needs evidence under its contract/context; this rationale does not promise that every bare string always resolves or install a resolver.

---

# 6. Identity Domain Constraints

The two original Identity Domain constraints retain DID-C-009–010. Domain membership supplies governing semantic qualification, not a mutable Family/Type label, folder or repository boundary.

---

## 6.1. DID-C-009 — Domain Membership

Each applicable assigned document identity shall have one governing Identity Domain under its allocation/preservation contract. Domain owner, canonical qualification/rules and actual uniqueness/reservation scope shall be explicit.

Other entity kinds or external domains retain their own qualified contracts; they are not automatically additional identities of this same document under this contract. Domain representation prefix and full qualified semantic subject remain distinct. A declared domain alone proves no actual collision-free allocation.

---

### 6.1.1. Rationale

An explicit governing domain identifies the scope and responsible rules for uniqueness and preservation. Actual population/history and authority evidence determines the assessed claim.

---

## 6.2. DID-C-010 — Domain Stability

Ordinary evolution shall preserve the assigned governing domain/key association. Repository, format, classification, status or edition changes do not silently move an identity to another domain.

A necessary change affecting the domain/allocation contract first requires §12 previous/new governing-rule and responsible-authority reconciliation, actual source/consumer impact, old→new qualification/mappings, collisions/aliases/reservations/history and intended reference/exact-snapshot continuity before coordinated application. No silent domain reassignment, arbitrary key replacement, reuse for another document or historical snapshot retargeting is permitted. This UPDATE executes no domain migration.

---

### 6.2.1. Rationale

Changing governing qualification can affect uniqueness, interpretation and consumers. Explicit prior/new assessment prevents an unrecorded domain change from being mistaken for an ordinary descriptor/location update.

---

# 7. Reference Constraints

The two original Reference constraints retain DID-C-011–012. Typed connection/endpoint semantics and reference records remain with their responsible owners; identity defines document-target meaning.

---

## 7.1. DID-C-011 — Reference Validity

Each actual document-targeting reference shall identify its intended existing qualified Domain+Identifier logical document, or exact edition with the additional coordinates/bytes and context required by its responsible contract. Non-document endpoints follow their own typed identity contracts; not every architectural reference is a document endpoint.

Incoming reference population may be0..N; a key does not require an incoming reference merely to exist. Optional incoming cardinality does not waive validity of each actual reference. Record actual target/alias interpretation and dangling, ambiguous, stale or unavailable observations. Distinguish preserved historical interpretation from current live retrieval and full connection validity. No perpetual availability guarantee, silent identity creation or target substitution is allowed.

---

### 7.1.1. Rationale

Valid document-targeting references identify the intended existing subject/context rather than invented or ambiguous keys. Other endpoint kinds retain their contracts, and actual performed checks determine observed resolution within coverage limits.

---

## 7.2. DID-C-012 — Reference Independence

References shall not allocate, redefine or replace their intended document identity. Relationships owns connection meaning and records; Registry registration, Knowledge Graph projection and Metadata descriptors remain with their respective owners.

Mutable reference/projection/location records may evolve under applicable rules without changing the document key. Never silently retarget an immutable historical Baseline member or create a key to make a check pass. Identity semantic ownership remains subject to common Architecture/Policy and responsible domain authority; it does not acquire every related record or grant operational permission.

---

### 7.2.1. Rationale

Document Identity owns document-key/domain meaning under applicable governing rules. Preserving other connection/record owners and intended targets prevents a reference representation from becoming competing identity authority.

---

# 8. Architectural Constraints

The six original independence constraints retain DID-C-013–018. They separate logical identity semantics from implementation choices; they do not prohibit legitimate governed representation/interface constraints or remove actual implementation evidence/consumer responsibilities. No separate historic rationale blocks are invented for these six constraints.

---

## 8.1. DID-C-013 — Technology Independence

Document-key/domain meaning shall not be silently redefined by technology choices. Explicit justified logical representation, interface or integration constraints remain legitimate under applicable owner contracts. Actual implementations require assessed adapters, compatibility and evidence; semantic independence guarantees no universal technology suitability.

---

## 8.2. DID-C-014 — Repository Independence

Repository location/custody shall not redefine an assigned logical key. Moving a representation can affect links, indexes, permissions and freshness under their own contracts; assess actual old/new targets and records without reallocating the document automatically. No always-available repository service is inferred.

---

## 8.3. DID-C-015 — Storage Independence

Storage mechanism shall not redefine logical document identity. Persistence and retrieval implementations preserve applicable canonical interpretation, source/edition/context provenance and historical evidence under their contracts. Storage/index record changes are not automatically key changes; real persistence or future availability needs observations.

---

## 8.4. DID-C-016 — Format Independence

Document format or serialization shall preserve the intended qualified identity meaning across legitimate representations. Domain canonical syntax and declared logical schemas/interfaces may constrain representations; technology independence does not exempt them from actual compatibility checks. Necessary representation migration follows §12 and preserves historical exact-snapshot interpretation; no automatic key reallocation is allowed.

---

## 8.5. DID-C-017 — Programming Language Independence

Programming-language choices shall not define competing document-key/domain semantics. Actual implementations can use language-specific structures/adapters while preserving governed meaning, representation/interface requirements and evidence. No language runtime or fully compatible implementation is supplied or certified here.

---

## 8.6. DID-C-018 — Implementation Independence

Implementation decisions shall not silently replace responsible identity semantics or waive common governing contracts. Owner-defined logical meaning and explicitly applicable interfaces constrain implementations; actual executor, inputs/outputs, rules, checks and observed limits require evidence. Legitimate domain-preserving adapters are distinct from implementation-specific semantic redefinition. No complete interoperability or independent-consumer rollout is guaranteed.

---

# 9. Cross-Component Constraints

The six original cross-component subjects remain. Semantic ownership, record ownership, documentary authority, required consumption, projection/navigation and actual execution are distinct. Actual required dependencies identify consumer→provider contract, scope, responsible source editions and interfaces under ARC-004/005; a documentary reference alone is not an operational call or complete required graph.

---

## 9.1. Metadata

Metadata owns descriptor/model/schema/profile/instance contracts; Document Identity owns document-key meaning. Metadata→Document Identity is the required identification claim for the applicable normalized document described, not every Metadata entity.

The functional DID README states: “The Document Identity component depends on the Metadata component for the canonical definition of metadata concepts used to describe document identity.” DID-009§5.1.1/§10 retains this actual Document Identity→Metadata claim alongside Metadata→Document Identity. Keep both reciprocal requirements explicit pending responsible core-versus-descriptor/interface/source-edition reconciliation. Different scope names, projections or relabelling as navigation do not dissolve a genuine required cycle. No globally acyclic graph is certified here.

Descriptor records can represent identity-related facts without redefining the key or inventing absent mandatory Metadata definitions. Full State/Canonical Reference authority remains pending under §12.

---

## 9.2. Classification

Classification owns category meaning and assignments. Classification→Document Identity supplies the intended applicable normalized document key when classifying a document. Category/definition/assignment entity keys follow their own contracts. Current Family/Type/Component changes do not regenerate the stable allocated document series/key. Classification does not silently redefine document identity.

---

## 9.3. Registry

Registry owns document registration/index records and uses intended qualified identity plus required source edition/context, provenance and freshness. Registry→Document Identity for document registration and Registry→Metadata for descriptors are selected actual contracts, not a universal intermediary route. Registration is not allocation; repeated entries/copies do not alone prove colliding assignments or complete population coverage. Registry does not acquire identity meaning or approval authority.

---

## 9.4. Relationships

Relationships owns typed connections, endpoint meaning and provenance. Document endpoints use intended qualified document/exact-edition contracts in §7; other endpoints retain their own identities. Creating or changing a connection does not allocate/redefine document identity or grant arbitrary target substitution. Connection validity and observed target retrieval are distinct; required provider contracts remain required even if data arrives through a projection.

---

## 9.5. Knowledge Graph

Knowledge Graph owns logical node/edge projection and properties with authoritative source/edition/context provenance and refresh limits. Knowledge Graph→Document Identity for document-node meaning and Knowledge Graph→Relationships for typed connections remain selected actual contracts. Node/property/projection records may evolve while preserving intended authoritative identity and connection interpretation; no competing allocation/semantic authority is created.

Logical projection/interface requirements are architectural responsibilities; storage/runtime choices remain implementation concerns. Projection is not proof of complete graph correctness, global acyclicity or synchronized consumers.

---

## 9.6. Governance

Governance is the area grouping Workflow, Policies, Reviews and Baselines documentary contracts. Actual operations belong to the applicable DMS, tool or manual executor, with CMS governing changes in its scope. Record actual authority/decision, responsible rules/source editions, exact subject/context, executor and observed results; authorship, custody or a local PASS alone grants no operational permission.

Preserve assigned same-document key through ordinary document evolution while supporting lifecycle/state/descriptor records follow their owners. DID-006's selected eight-transition contract is not a universal permission graph; document Status, file/edition/index deletion or archiving alone does not allocate/retire a logical key or grant an unlisted edge. Retirement needs its own actual responsible decision/scope and retained reservations/history.

Baselines requires exact eligible approved editions, actual selection evidence and relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Logical identity alone does not select a member. Draft successors do not inherit approval, publication or Baseline membership and do not retarget immutable historical snapshots. Review, validation, approval, publication, identity lifecycle and document Status/edition remain distinct.

---

# 12. Compliance

An actual conformance claim shall identify its exact subject/domain, artifacts/editions/bytes and context, applicable responsible mandatory rules/source editions/interfaces, executor/method, performed/unperformed checks, observations, population/coverage and limitations. Evaluate every applicable mandatory requirement of that declared claim; justify inapplicability explicitly rather than omitting requirements to manufacture success.

DID-007 distinguishes Valid, Invalid, Inconsistent and Unresolvable observations. A successful subset is narrower check evidence, not full identity/component/framework conformity. Establish an actual violation through its applicable rule, subject/context and observed nonconformance. Missing evidence or unresolved authority is neither unconditional success nor automatic Invalid/Unresolvable; preserve all supported negative observations and their limits without suppressing them through a silent precedence rule.

Actual mandatory State/Canonical Reference and complete-record/lifecycle claims in DID-014§§7–8/15/18 remain pending owner reconciliation with DID-005§6 and DID-006. The selected key/association scope does not remove mandatory peer fields, invent an accepted merged record/state machine or approve disregarding another responsible contract. Withhold broader conformity where applicable mandatory evidence/authority is unresolved; narrower unambiguous observations retain their limits. Local source correction validation does not close full peer propagation, reciprocal Metadata/Identity requirements or complete graph/implementation conformity.

The three received conditions for ordinary additional implementation constraints remain:

- do not contradict this specification;
- preserve backward compatibility;
- maintain the canonical architectural model.

These concern ordinary compatible additions under applicable responsible contracts; an implementation extension is not authority to silently amend canonical semantics. DID-014§14 also requires additive/backward-compatible extensions and states that core identity semantics are not extensible. Preserve that actual restriction and its owner-reconciliation obligation; this local correction does not waive it or assert universal agreement with the controlled-evolution protocol.

Before any necessary normative contract or identity/domain/path/representation transition:

1. Preserve original artifacts, actual observations and failed checks; identify prior/new responsible rules/editions, rationale, actual authority and intended subjects/context. A finding, local PASS or documentary authorship alone grants no mutation, allocation or approval.
2. Assess affected semantic/record owners, consumers, indispensable consumer→provider interfaces and unresolved mandatory field/state/extension/required-cycle claims. Reconcile conflicting governing authority before claiming integrated conformance; different names or projection labels cannot remove a real required edge.
3. Record compatibility, exact old→new mappings/qualification, canonical aliases, collisions/reservations/history, same-document continuity and intended references/exact-edition/pinned-snapshot context. Never reassign an allocated/retired key to another document or retarget immutable historical members.
4. Apply only the separately authorized scoped change with actual contributor/event provenance and coordinated transition evidence. For changed working documents, compatible correction retains Version, compatible additive capability increments minor, incompatible contract change increments major and resets minor to0; every persisted changed edition increments Revision monotonically across Versions. Other entity allocation/lifecycle contracts remain separate.
5. Validate resulting exact artifacts/editions in the subsequent appropriate operation and record observations/coverage/remaining conflicts. Unchanged-source validation changes neither source coordinate; later changed bytes need their own assessment. Do not rewrite previous pending events or failures as historical successes.

Evaluation is distinct from writing a result record and from authorized correction; no silent repair/allocation/migration is performed here. Normative intent, received Canonical naming, a Draft working source, local review/validation or implemented check result is not global architectural approval, operational permission, publication or Baseline selection.

# 7. Canonical Elements

Every Document Identity is composed of the following canonical elements.

| Element | Description | Mandatory |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| Document Identity | Permanent architectural identity | Yes |
| Identifier | Canonical identifier | Yes |
| Identity Domain | Scope of uniqueness | Yes |
| Identity State | Lifecycle state | Yes |

The canonical schema is defined conceptually as follows.

```text

                    Document Identity
                    ├── Identifier
                    ├── Identity Domain
                    ├── Lifecycle State
                    └── Canonical Reference

```

The schema defines the logical organisation of identity information.

It does not prescribe any implementation format.

# 12. Relationship Specification

| Component | Relationship |
|-----------|--------------|
| Metadata | Describes identified documents. |
| Classification | Classifies identified documents. |
| Templates | Defines document structures independently of identity. |
| Registry | Registers canonical identities. |
| Relationships | Associates identified documents. |

| Governance | Operates on identified documents. |

# 18. Conformance Statement

An implementation claiming conformance with the Documentation Framework **Document Identity** component shall satisfy every mandatory requirement defined by this specification and by all normative references listed herein.

No implementation-specific optimisation, extension, or integration shall modify the canonical semantics of a Document Identity.

# 12. Layer Dependencies

A required dependency is directed **consumer→provider**: the consumer needs the stated provider contract in the declared scope. Allocation, documentary authority reference, semantic association, data projection, navigation and execution order are separately typed and must not be inferred solely from row order or arrows.

For cross-Layer required contracts governed here, the support order is Foundation, Architecture, Documentation, Governance, Discovery, Automation, Integration. Lower means an earlier support area in this declared order, not a lower visual row. A consumer's cross-Layer required provider belongs to an earlier support area. This does not require every consumer to depend on every earlier Layer or form an adjacent serial chain. Same-Layer required contracts are permitted under explicit ownership/interfaces and the cycle rule. Changing this structural constraint requires assessed architectural revision under §17, not an unrecorded upward-dependency exception.

| Consumer | Consumer area | Provider | Provider area | Required contract | Scope/justification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Registry | Discovery | Metadata | Documentation | Descriptive values with source-edition provenance | When indexing edition descriptors; refresh or identify stale values |
| Knowledge Graph | Discovery | Document Identity | Documentation | Entity identity for logical document nodes | When keying document nodes; other entity kinds use their own endpoint identity contracts |
| Knowledge Graph | Discovery | Relationships | Discovery | Typed connection records and provenance | When projecting the semantic network and interpreting dependency kinds |

Governance defines documentary lifecycle, policy, review and immutable snapshot contracts. It does not itself prove an implemented process engine. Exact-edition review, validation, approval, publication and membership are distinct decisions/events.

---

## 6.1. Workflow

### 6.1.1. Purpose

Defines exact-edition lifecycle, transition, responsibility and evidence contracts.

---

### 6.1.2. Responsibilities

Describe documentary state transitions and publication conditions under applicable Policies. A DMS, tool or manual process executes operations; CMS governs changes in its own scope. Logical identity, Version/Revision, exact Status, approval/publication and membership are separate. ## 6.2. Policies

### 6.2.1. Purpose

Defines applicable documentary governance rules and evidence requirements.

---

### 6.2.2. Responsibilities

State review, publication, approval and maintenance policies with applicability and responsible authorities. Rules govern identified editions and operations; actual author contribution, authorization, review, validation and approval remain distinct. Policy definition does not prove implementation, grant an operation automatically or replace semantic owners in other domains.

---

## 6.3. Reviews

### 6.3.1. Purpose

Defines review responsibilities and records examined scope, observations and findings.

---

### 6.3.2. Responsibilities

Technical and architectural review assess exact identified artifacts/rules and consistency within recorded coverage. Reviews may use results from Validation or Consistency Verification, whose executors record applicable checks; overlapping check domains do not create competing semantics or approval authority. A review result is evidence, not an approval, publication decision, Baseline selection or guarantee of product consequences.

## 6.4. Baselines

### 6.4.1. Purpose

Defines separately identified immutable selections of exact approved document editions.

---

### 6.4.2. Responsibilities

Preserve explicit selected member identity/edition coordinates and relevant pinned relationship context or traceable verification evidence. Release snapshots and historical traceability require scope and selection evidence; a current path or time label alone is insufficient. # 7. Discovery Components

Discovery defines typed connections, catalog/network projections and access to identified entities/editions. Directories remain physical locations rather than semantic authority. Draft, historical and snapshot-specific discovery is allowed with explicit state and scope; discoverability does not confer approval.

## 7.1. Registry

### 7.1.1. Purpose

Defines catalog/lookup authority for its declared entity/edition scope.

---

### 7.1.2. Responsibilities

Support registration, lookup and discoverability through traceable authoritative source-edition records/projections. ## 7.2. Relationships

### 7.2.1. Purpose

Defines typed connection records for identified endpoints and their provenance.

### 7.2.2. Responsibilities

Map and preserve semantic reference, association, replacement, navigation and required-dependency kinds as applicable. Endpoint domains and identity contracts follow their entity kinds; not every endpoint gets a normalized document ID. Required edges use consumer→provider contract/scope and remain visible, including genuine cycles requiring reconciliation. Explicit records support traceability without fabricating a complete relation catalog.

## 7.3. Knowledge Graph

### 7.3.1. Purpose

Defines traceable semantic-network projections of identified entities and typed Relationships records.

---

### 7.3.2. Responsibilities

Support semantic navigation, dependency and impact analysis with authoritative source/edition provenance. Derived values do not acquire competing semantic authority; views declare refresh/freshness and current/historical/snapshot scope. No universal Registry-to-Graph routing or complete network/acyclicity is inferred from this capability.

## 7.4. Navigation

### 7.4.1. Purpose

Defines logical access through declared entity/edition and relationship views.

### 7.4.2. Responsibilities

# 8. Automation Components

Automation defines intended repeatable checking/generation capabilities. Applicable implementations consume authoritative owner contracts on identified inputs and provide execution evidence; architectural definitions alone establish neither installed tools nor verified outcomes.

### 8.1.1. Purpose

Defines scoped evaluation of identified requirements against exact artifacts/editions.

---

### 8.1.2. Responsibilities

Cover Metadata, identity, relationship and consistency requirements supplied by their responsible owners. Actual execution records inputs, rules, checks, observations, coverage, executor and limits. A PASS neither guarantees global correctness nor approves/publishes/selects a Baseline; subsequent changed bytes need their own assessment.

---

## 8.2. Metadata Generator

### 8.2.1. Purpose

Defines generation/completion/synchronization of descriptor representations under applicable owner rules.

---

### 8.2.2. Responsibilities

Identify exact inputs, output edition/representation, applicable Dictionary/Schema/Profile and provenance. Completion derives or requests values through declared rules; it is not permission to invent absent identity, category, lifecycle or approval facts. Generated values require applicable constraint assessment and synchronization/refresh evidence. Capability definition alone proves no implemented generator or successful result.

## 8.3. Registry Generator

### 8.3.1. Purpose

Defines creation/update of scoped Registry projections from authoritative source records/editions.

---

### 8.3.2. Responsibilities

Declare source/input and generated-output provenance, applicable catalog/owner rules and refresh/current-stale handling. Consistency checks state examined records, coverage and limits; generation does not replace domain or relationship-record authority. ## 8.4. Documentation Generator

### 8.4.1. Purpose

Defines generation of documentary artifacts from identified definitions/inputs.

---

### 8.4.2. Responsibilities

## 8.5. Consistency Verification

### 8.5.1. Purpose

Defines scoped cross-record/contract verification under applicable authoritative requirements.

---

### 8.5.2. Responsibilities

Shared check domains with Validation/Reviews do not imply competing rule ownership or global integrity; a partial matrix cannot certify the complete framework graph.

---

# 9. Integration Components

Integration defines optional use-case adapters to supported external environments and interfaces. Adapters consume owner/authorization contracts without becoming new semantic owners or approvers. Describing integration does not establish its implementation, completeness, performance or mandatory use.

---

## 9.1. Source Control Integration

### 9.1.1. Purpose

Defines an adapter to supported source-control provenance and versioned representations. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

### 9.2.1. Purpose

Defines delivery-pipeline adapters executing scoped checks and authorized publication for identified editions. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

### 9.3.1. Purpose

Defines supported authoring/development adapters under applicable representation and owner contracts. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

## 9.4. Documentation Platform Integration

### 9.4.1. Purpose

Defines platform publication adapters following Governance authorization for the exact edition. Actual adapter availability and executed results require implementation evidence; no automatic approval or mandatory ecosystem is inferred.

## 9.5. AI Integration

### 9.5.1. Purpose

Defines assisted reasoning/authoring against identified domain contracts and source evidence. A required dependency is directed **consumer→provider** and identifies the provider contract needed in a declared scope. Documentary authority reference, semantic association, projection, navigation and execution are distinct meanings; visual position does not identify required edges.
